# Advances in Automated Line Inspections

Corvin Talvbrook: Welcome back to The Tavley Briefing. Today, we’re diving into the latest advances in automated line inspections, especially how drones are reshaping wildfire risk management. Joining me is Quillan Heskmoor, lead engineer at AeroVigil, a company pioneering these technologies. Quillan, great to have you here.

Quillan Heskmoor: Thanks, Corvin. Excited to chat about this—it’s a field moving faster than most realize.

Corvin Talvbrook: Let’s start with the big picture. How have drone inspections evolved in the past two years?

Quillan Heskmoor: Well, two years ago, most drones were limited to visual imaging, kind of like birds-eye photos. But now, thanks to breakthroughs in hyperspectral sensors and onboard AI, they’re not just capturing images—they’re analyzing vegetation health, identifying stressed trees near power lines in near real-time. For example, last fall, we flew a 30-drone swarm over the Wexley Ridge corridor. The system flagged 120 high-risk trees that had fungal infections invisible to the naked eye.

Corvin Talvbrook: That’s impressive. How does this impact crew safety and efficiency?

Quillan Heskmoor: Tremendously. Instead of sending line crews into potentially hazardous terrain blindly, we provide precise, data-driven maps. In one pilot project near Lakeford, drone-driven inspections cut line inspection time by 40% and reduced worker exposure to wildfire zones by over 60%. It’s a game changer.

Corvin Talvbrook: Any challenges still holding back widespread adoption?

Quillan Heskmoor: Definitely. Regulatory hurdles remain a big one. Also, integrating data from drone flights with existing utility management platforms is complex. But with ongoing investments and collaborations, I’m optimistic 2025 will see many utilities fully embrace these tools.

Corvin Talvbrook: Thanks, Quillan. Fascinating insights into a technology that’s literally changing the landscape of wildfire prevention.
